user_summary: This batch has the same trap as last time, but more often. Items 2, 3, 4, 9, 10, 13 and 14 all cite a prior result that exists somewhere in the study, just not in the report they're paired with. The repeated proposals (12/17 and 14/16) are useful checks on the automated judge. In each pair, one report shares the proposal's topic but contradicts its premise. That's exactly where a judge that matches on vocabulary would wrongly answer yes.
